_: POLICY — the decisions the plan takes about money, stated once.
These are not forecasts. They are the rules the institution will run
by: how fees are collected and refunded, what the reserve is for and
how large it must be, how much cash the College keeps in hand, and how

fxUsdPerGbp.s: Mean of the twelve HMRC monthly exchange rates for the US dollar, October 2025 to September 2026 (1.3126 to 1.3647). HMRC monthly exchange rates — trade-tariff.service.gov.uk/exchange_rates, retrieved 23 Sep 2026. The College earns in dollars and pays in pounds; a stronger pound is tested as a named shock

cardShareOfRetail.s: Share of learner fees paid by card; the balance by bank transfer

ukStandard.s: Standard UK cards, 1.5% + 20p. Stripe, UK pricing — stripe.com/gb/pricing, retrieved 23 Sep 2026

ukPremium.s: Premium UK cards, 2.8% + 20p. Stripe, UK pricing — stripe.com/gb/pricing, retrieved 23 Sep 2026

eea.s: EEA cards, 2.5% + 20p. Stripe, UK pricing — stripe.com/gb/pricing, retrieved 23 Sep 2026

international.s: International cards, 3.15% + 20p. Stripe, UK pricing — stripe.com/gb/pricing, retrieved 23 Sep 2026

conversion.s: An additional 2% where currency conversion is required. Fees are charged in dollars and the College settles in pounds, so the plan charges it on every card payment. Stripe, UK pricing — stripe.com/gb/pricing, retrieved 23 Sep 2026

fixedGbp.s: 20p per successful card payment. Stripe, UK pricing — stripe.com/gb/pricing, retrieved 23 Sep 2026

paymentsPerLevel.s: Most learners pay each level in one payment; some by instalment

billedAhead.s: Fees are billed per level, at the start of the level. A learner never pays for a level before it begins, so the College holds no untaught fees in advance

withdrawalRate.s: Share of level starts withdrawn inside the fourteen-day window, refunded in full

indexation.s: Fees rise each year with the cost of the people who deliver them

roundingUsd.s: A level fee is stated to the nearest fifty dollars

onePriceWorldwide.s: A route costs the same wherever the learner lives. The College's response to a market that cannot pay for a route is to offer it there through an institutional buyer, not to sell it more cheaply

pricingVolumeYear.s: Institutional costs are absorbed over the volume the plan reaches at maturity, not over the thin first years; the difference is what the founding capital is for

targetMonths.s: Six months of operating cost held as an institutional reserve — enough to teach every enrolled learner to the end of the level they have begun and to meet a year in which enrolment falls and cost does not

minimumMonths.s: The College never plans to hold less than three months of operating cost in cash

payrollLeadTerms.s: An instructor is hired and paid from the term before the learners who need them arrive

returnBy.s: The plan must be able to return the founding capital by the end of its tenth year while holding its reserve at target

form.s: The form of the founding capital — equity, loan, grant or a combination — is a decision reserved to the founders and the Board. The plan sizes the requirement and the gates against which it is released; it does not assume the form
